title: Exceptional by Design: Long-Range Hopping as a Knob for Exceptional Point Control
authors: Carolina Martinez-Strasser, Dario Bercioux, Nico Leumer
abstract: Exceptional points are degeneracies unique to non-Hermitian systems, where eigenvalues and eigenvectors coalesce, rendering the Hamiltonian defective. We investigate the exceptional-point structure and topological properties of a generalized non-Hermitian Rice-Mele model with balanced gain and loss, as well as next-nearest-neighbor hopping. The system hosts only second-order exceptional points under both periodic and open boundary conditions. Under periodic boundary conditions, the exceptional points in parameter space lie on lines and ellipses that are independent of the next-nearest-neighbor hopping, since the latter enters the bulk Hamiltonian only as an identity contribution. Under open boundary conditions, this independence is broken: the next-nearest-neighbor hopping not only shifts the energy of existing exceptional points but also generates new ones, with a specific condition signaling a topological gap closing observed only in the open-boundary spectrum. At special parameter points, multiple simultaneous second-order exceptional points yield degenerate configurations whose degeneracy grows with system size. Exceptional point locations are identified numerically via the condition number of the eigenvector matrix and confirmed by Jordan decomposition. The topological phase diagram, computed via a winding number framework for non-Hermitian systems without symmetry protection, reveals sectors with zero, one, and two edge states; the bulk-boundary correspondence is confirmed, and the non-Hermitian skin effect is absent.
summary: This paper analyzes the topological phase diagram of a non-Hermitian lattice model by studying its exceptional points (EPs) under periodic versus open boundary conditions. It demonstrates that long-range hopping terms significantly alter the EP structure in OBC compared to PBC, while confirming the existence and characterization of topologically protected edge states using winding numbers.
main_problem: The study investigates the exceptional point (EP) structure and topological properties of non-Hermitian lattice models, specifically focusing on how long-range hopping terms modify these features under different boundary conditions.
main_result: The model exhibits second-order EPs whose dependence on next-nearest-neighbor hopping ($m$) differs significantly between periodic and open boundary conditions; furthermore, topological edge states are confirmed via winding number analysis in OBC.
method: Theoretical analysis combining numerical computation (condition number, Jordan decomposition) with analytical tools like the winding number framework and M-Riemann algebra formalism to map out parameter space degeneracies.
model_or_system: A generalized non-Hermitian Rice-Mele model described by a 1D tight-binding Hamiltonian incorporating intra-cell hopping ($t$), inter-cell hopping ($t'$), next-nearest-neighbor hopping ($m$), and gain/loss terms ($\pm i\gamma$).
key_observables: Exceptional Points (EPs), topological invariants (winding number $W_j$), edge state eigenvalues, and the Directional Inverse Participation Ratio (dIPR).
important_parameters: Hopping ratios ($t/t'$, $m/\gamma$), boundary conditions (PBC vs. OBC), and system size ($N$).
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on second-order EPs, and specific symmetries are assumed or broken to simplify the topological classification.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate EP structures as lines/ellipses in parameter space for both PBC and OBC; phase diagrams map out edge state regimes using winding numbers and dIPR values.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the Hamiltonian, first establishing bulk properties under PBC (independence of $m$), then contrasting this with OBC where $m$ actively generates new EPs. Finally, it uses topological invariants and localization measures to confirm boundary-induced edge states.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses non-Hermitian physics, a field highly relevant to open quantum systems, wave propagation in lossy media, and engineered photonic/electronic structures where gain/loss are inherent.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Sketch of the model in real space. (a) SSH chain with t, t′ for intra- and inter-cell hopping, and m for long-range hopping terms. Sublattice A (B) sites, shown in blue (red), encode gain/loss ±iγ and on-site energies ϵA,B. The gray box indicates the unit cell. (b) The system is rep- resented as a quantum ladder, with sublattices coupled by t and t′. (c) Real space distances of panel (b) in terms of the lattice constant d.

Figure 2. Bulk complex spectrum and exceptional points. Bulk energy spectrum of H(k) in the complex plane, parametrized by k ∈BZ, for fixed ϵ+ = t′ and ϵ−= 0. Each panel shows three superposed spectra corresponding to m = 0 (red), m = t′ (blue), and m = 2t′ (orange). Parameters: (a) t = t′/2, γ = 1.4 t′; (b) t = t′/2, γ = 1.6 t′; (c) t = 3t′/2, γ = 1.4 t′; (d) t = 3t′/2, γ = 1.6 t′. For m = 0, the spectrum is purely imaginary (up to the constant real shift ϵ+), while for m ̸= 0, the next-nearest-neighbor hopping introduces a k-dependent dispersion of the real part, producing genuinely complex bands. Green stars mark the bulk EPs, which lie on the real axis at Re (EEP) = ϵ+ −2m cos(kEPd)....

Figure 3. Finite-size EPs under PBC and OBC. (a) For PBC, the 10-base logarithm of the condition matrix K(U) diverges at EPs. These divergences coincide with the analytic result from Eq. (8) (black dashed lines). For odd N, the lines with positive slopes t ± γ are absent. For N > 2, the EPs form ellipses and rings. (a) N = 2, (b) N = 3, (c) N = 4, (d) N = 9, and (e) N = 10. In all the panels ϵ± = 0 and m = 0. Note that these results are m-independent, since the value of m only changes the degeneracy energy at the EPs. Note as well that for N = 9, 10, we indicate only the analytic lines corresponding to ±t ± γ.
